definition: Euphemism means a mild or indirect expression substituted for a harsh or blunt one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word euphemism. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know euphemism should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Real-estate listings run on euphemism: 'cozy' for cramped, 'vintage charm' for a furnace older than your grandmother.
A hedge is milder than a euphemism — the speaker just goes vague ('we'll see,' 'at some point') and never offers the substitute phrase a euphemism supplies.
A whitewash goes further than a euphemism — softening becomes covering: the unpleasant fact isn't re-worded, it's painted over and denied.

An understatement admits the fact but shrinks it in the telling — 'a bit breezy' for a hurricane plays the size down. A euphemism keeps the fact at full size and swaps in kinder wording for it. Understatement cuts the thing down; a euphemism re-dresses it.

A code word is an insider's substitute, built to exclude outsiders — secrecy is its whole job. A euphemism is a substitute anyone present can decode; its job is to soften the blow, not to keep the topic from the uninitiated.

openness that skips the softening entirely

Euphemism is the precise term because each phrase is a mild or indirect expression substituted for a harsh or blunt one — the drill does not stop being a drill, but the word stops announcing it.
A white lie changes the facts; a euphemism keeps the facts and swaps out their clothes.
Euphemism names the softened phrase itself — use it when the wording is doing the cushioning.
